content.text: caused by focal brain, spinal cord, or retinal ischemia

▪︎causes: macrovascular (carotid artery stenosis), microvascular (small-vessel atherosclerosis/vasculitis in brain or retinal artery), cardiac (AFib, cardiomyopathy, valvular dz), noncardiac (sickle cell dz, systemic thrombophilic d/o)
▪︎acute neuro compromise that resolves on its own w/o tissue damage; time no longer used in TIA definition (most resolve w/in 24 hrs, but a few min of ischemia can cause permanent damage)
Neuroimaging + neurovasc imaging + r/o cardioembolic source
Place pt in supine position to increase cerebral perf, ⍉lowering BP unless >220/120

▪︎moderate–high risk → aspirin + clopidogrel (DAPT) daily x21 days while awaiting imaging; aspirin 160–325 mg load then 50–100 mg daily; clopidogrel 300–600 mg load then 75 mg daily; combo more protective than either alone
▪︎10% have stroke w/in 90 days; ABCD² developed to predict 2-day risk but controversial (may not be best predictor)
▪︎risk groups (original validated cutoffs): 0-3 low, 4-5 moderate, 6-7 high
recommended if internal carotid a. stenosis
▪︎lipid-lowering (statin) if ↑cholesterol, high CV risk, or atherosclerosis

Acute onset of neurological deficits ← death of brain tissue from ischemia
▪︎ischemic CVA (MC): thrombus, embolus, or systemic hypoperfusion (massive blood loss, obstructive shock); hemorrhagic = ICH or SAH
: (1/3) commonly come from ♡, aortic arch, or lrg cerebral arteries –
▪︎+ atherosclerosis, valvular dz, hypercoagulable d/o, vasculitis; cocaine
– aphasia, neglect, hemiparesis, gaze preference, homonymous hemianopsia
– coma, CN palsies, apnea, drop attack, vertigo
▪︎Wallenberg (lateral medullary) infarct: dizziness, difficulty sitting upright, diplopia, nystagmus, ipsilateral arm ataxia + loss of pain/temp in ipsilateral face + contralateral trunk/limbs
(bilateral forehead innervation); Bell palsy (peripheral) → ⍉forehead wrinkling + eyebrow droop
– best initial to r/o hemorrhagic CVA;
▪︎MRI: more sensitive than CT for acute ischemic stroke (but not often initial test in ED – time-consuming, expensive, less available)
▪︎CT findings: loss of gray-white interface, acute hypodensity; rule out hypoglycemia; NIHSS for severity
▪︎⍉contrast CT in acute ischemic stroke eval; transcranial Doppler assesses vessel patency but ⍉sensitive for acute ischemia

▪︎rule out embolic Eti if large infarct, hemorrhagic conversion, multiple or multi-territory infarcts; pt <45yo w/ suspected embolic stroke → cardiac workup (monitoring + TEE: r/o AFib, valvular dz, PFO)
▪︎hypercoagulable workup: personal/family hx systemic thrombosis, young pt w/o clear Eti, lupus/antiphospholipid Ab
▪︎large artery occlusion in proximal anterior circulation → mechanical thrombectomy (possible w/in 24 hrs; DAWN/DEFUSE 3 risk-stratify)
▪︎high-dose statin + antiplatelet (aspirin) started w/in 48 hrs, as soon as oral meds safe
